solves.reasoning: (A) pioneer fits 'study of animal biology' context, not follower. (B) nutrition matches 'animal nutrition and metabolism'. (C) outstanding fits positive context of teacher.
(A) conduct fits 'came to UC Davis to conduct research'. (B) distinguished fits award context. (C) subsequently fits time sequence after 1961 publication.
(A) earned fits 'earned his doctoral degree'. (B) translated fits 'translated into German...'. (C) popular fits 'popular with undergraduates'.
③ withdrew means 'left/dropped out' but original is 'graduated'. He graduated from the institute, not withdrew.
② banned means 'prohibited' but original is 'published'. The book was published in 1961, not banned.
④ disgrace means 'shame' but original is 'honor'. The building was named in his honor, not disgrace.
The passage mentions 'energy metabolism in animals' later, and 'animal nutrition and ___' clearly needs metabolism.
The Borden Award is described positively with 'received' context. Distinguished fits an award of prestige.
Published in 1961 AND then translated = subsequently (afterward). Previously/simultaneously/rarely don't fit the chronological order.
Outstanding means exceptionally good. Excellent is the closest synonym. Average, ordinary, terrible are antonyms.
Conduct research = carry out research. Give up, put off, turn down all mean something different.
Earned his degree = obtained/achieved his degree. Lost, rejected, donated are opposite or unrelated.
Popular means well-liked. Despised (hated/scorned) is the opposite. Famous, beloved, favored are similar to popular.
Distinguished means renowned/notable. Obscure (unknown) is the antonym. Renowned, prestigious, eminent are synonyms.
(A) conduct research = 수행하다 (verb). (B) excellent conduct = 행동 (noun). So the pair is 수행하다 — 행동.
'A person who is among the first to explore or develop something new' = pioneer. Researcher/professor/graduate don't emphasize 'first'.
Subsequent (adjective) needs to become an adverb to modify 'translated'. Subsequently = afterward.
'Research on animal ___ and metabolism' needs a noun. Nutritious (adjective) → nutrition (noun).
Building named 'in his honor' = to honor him. Against his will, by successor, for punishment don't fit positive context.
Original says 'popular with undergraduates and graduate students alike'. This exact phrase fits the blank.
